
In this section, we will practice data visualization using Python and the `matplotlib` and `seaborn` packages. Follow the steps below to create various types of plots.

Using the same script `2-data-wrangling-and-visualization.py` from the previous section, continue with the following tasks:

If you have imported pandas and read in the `crashes` dataset (either the demo `crashes.csv` or the real Leeds 2025 [`crashes-leeds.csv`](https://github.com/itsleeds/introds/releases/download/v2/crashes-leeds.csv) dataset), you can proceed to the next steps. You will need to import `matplotlib.pyplot` and `seaborn` as well.

::: {.callout-tip}
Want to switch to the real Leeds 2025 crash data here? Just swap your `read_csv()` line to:
```python
crashes = pd.read_csv("https://github.com/itsleeds/introds/releases/download/v2/crashes-leeds.csv")
```
All the tasks below work identically because it uses the same core column names (`casualty_type`, `casualty_age`, `vehicle_type`, `dark`).
:::

1. **Box Plot:**
   - Create a box plot to visualise the distribution of ages for different casualty types in the `crashes` dataset.
   - Use `sns.boxplot()` to create the box plot.
   - Add appropriate labels and a title to your plot (if using `crashes-leeds.csv`, `plt.xticks(rotation=30)` helps keep the category labels legible).
   - Save the box plot to a file named `age_boxplot.png` using `plt.savefig()`.
   - Display the plot with `plt.show()`.

2. **Bar Plot (Optional):**
   - Create a bar plot showing the count of casualties by `casualty_type` (e.g., pedestrian, cyclist, cat in the demo data, or car, pedestrian, cyclist, motorcycle, etc. in the Leeds 2025 data).
   - Use `sns.countplot()` or `value_counts().plot(kind='bar')`.
   - Add custom colours and transparency to the bars.
   - Add appropriate labels and a title.
   - Save the plot to a file named `casualty_barplot.png`.

3. **Export Your Plots:**
   - Save the box plot as a PNG file named `age_boxplot.png`.
   - Save the bar plot as a PNG file named `casualty_barplot.png`.
   - Check the documentation for `plt.savefig()` by typing `help(plt.savefig)` in the console.

4. **Bonus — Explore Extra Columns (Leeds 2025 dataset):**
   - If you are using `crashes-leeds.csv`, try creating a scatter plot of crash locations (`longitude` vs `latitude`) coloured by `casualty_severity` using `sns.scatterplot(data=crashes, x='longitude', y='latitude', hue='casualty_severity', alpha=0.6)`!
   - Or plot casualty counts by `speed_limit`.

### Starter Code (Debug Me!)

The plotting script below shows how to create and save both visualisations for either dataset — **but it contains 5 deliberate bugs and will not run as written**. Copy it into your script, run it, read each traceback, and fix the errors until both PNG files are created.

```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplt as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Choose your dataset (comment/uncomment one of the two lines below):
path = "data/crashes.csv"
# path = "https://github.com/itsleeds/introds/releases/download/v2/crashes-leeds.csv"

crashes = pd.read_csv(path)

# 1. Box plot: distribution of casualty ages by casualty type
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.boxplot(data=crashes, x="casualty_type", y="age", ax=ax)
plt.title("Casualty Age by Type"
plt.xlabel("Casualty Type")
plt.ylabel("Age")
plt.xticks(rotation=30)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("age_boxplot.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

# 2. Bar plot: count of casualties by casualty type
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.count_plot(data=crashes, x="casualty_type", color="steelblue", alpha=0.8, ax=ax)
plt.title("Number of Casualties by Type")
plt.xlabel("Casualty Type")
plt.ylabel("Count")
plt.xticks(rotation=30)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.save_fig("casualty_barplot.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

<details>
<summary>Hints (if you get stuck)</summary>

Look out for:

1. A missing closing parenthesis on a `plt.title(...)` call (`SyntaxError`).
2. A typo in the `matplotlib.pyplot` import (`ModuleNotFoundError`).
3. A wrong column name passed to `y=` in `sns.boxplot(...)` (`ValueError`).
4. Extra underscores in two function names (`sns.countplot` and `plt.savefig`).

</details>

**R version:** If you prefer R, the same exercises are available in R. Continue using the `2-data-wrangling-and-visualization.R` script (with either `crashes.csv` or `crashes-leeds.csv`), load `ggplot2` (part of `tidyverse`), and use `geom_boxplot()`, `geom_bar()`, and `ggsave()` to complete the same tasks.

<details>
<summary>R Starter Code (Debug Me! — 3 deliberate bugs)</summary>

```r
library(tidyverse)

# Choose your dataset:
path <- "data/crashes.csv"
# path <- "https://github.com/itsleeds/introds/releases/download/v2/crashes-leeds.csv"

crashes <- read_csv(path)

# 1. Box plot
p_box <- ggplot(crashes, aes(x = casualty_type, y = age)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Casualty Age by Type", x = "Casualty Type", y = "Age") +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("age_boxplot.png", plot = p_box, width = 8, height = 5)

# 2. Bar plot
p_bar <- ggplot(crashes, aes(x = casualty_type)) +
  geom_bars(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8)
  labs(title = "Number of Casualties by Type", x = "Casualty Type", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("casualty_barplot.png", plot = p_bar, width = 8, height = 5)
```

</details>
